Sacramento State Sees Significant Growth in Black Student Enrollment FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE June 19, 2026 Media Contact: Becky Repka Director of Marketing & Communications, Sacramento State becky.repka@csus.edu Sacramento State Sees Significant Growth in Black Student Enrollment, Reflecting Commitment to Student Success and Belonging As the nation commemorates Juneteenth, University highlights record growth, innovative programs and support for Black students SACRAMENTO, Calif. — As communities across the nation celebrate Juneteenth and reflect on the ongoing pursuit of opportunity, equity and progress, Sacramento State is highlighting significant growth in its Black student population and the programs helping students succeed. Since Fall 2023, Black student enrollment at Sacramento State has increased by 23%, and new Black student enrollment for Fall 2026 is anticipated to grow by an additional 10%, bringing the overall number to about 2,500, using federal reporting guidelines. Using broader identity-based reporting, accounting for students who identify with more than one race, Black student enrollment was about 11%, or 3,266 students as of Spring 2026 and is anticipated to grow to nearly 4,000 by fall. Sacramento State enrolls more Black students than any other California State University campus and was the first CSU to be designated a Black-Serving Institution by the California State Assembly. “The observance of Juneteenth is an opportunity to highlight the transformative power of education as a pathway to opportunity, making Sacramento State's continued growth among Black students and investment in programs such as the nation's first Black Honors College especially meaningful,” said Sacramento State Senior Vice President for Student Affairs and Inclusive Excellence Aniesha Mitchell. "The increase in enrollment among Black students reflects the culture we are intentionally building—one where all students are welcomed, supported and encouraged to thrive.” The enrollment growth reflects Sacramento State's continued focus on creating an environment where students are empowered to achieve their goals. This is demonstrated through the University's Black Honors College, the first of its kind in the nation, which has experienced remarkable growth since its launch. It nearly tripled in size in one year, growing from 77 students in Fall 2024 to 228 students in Fall 2025. The program anticipates continued growth for the Fall 2026 semester. "The growth of Sacramento State's Black Honors College demonstrates the impact of creating spaces where students feel seen, supported and connected," said Boatamo Mosupyoe, dean of students and chief administrative officer for Sacramento State's Black Honors College. "We are committed to supporting students throughout their journey at Sacramento State, helping them build connections, reach their goals, and graduate prepared to make an impact in their communities and careers." The Black Honors College provides students with academic enrichment, leadership development, mentorship opportunities, and a strong community focused on excellence and achievement. The program was created to support student success while fostering connections and belonging among participants. The College is designed to equip scholars with the necessary academic, professional, and personal skills needed for economic empowerment, self-determination, and courageous leadership. As part of the California State University system, the largest public university system in the world, Sacramento State is the sixth-largest campus, with more than 31,000 students, 91% of whom are undergraduates. Sacramento State’s mission is to transform lives by preparing students for leadership, service, and success.
